sections.instructionBn: Read the text and choose the correct answer. Write only the answer.
sections.stimulusMd:
Nusair and Samin are two friends. They go to Armanitola Government Primary School located in Old Dhaka. Every morning, they walk to school along the river Buriganga. On their way, they see people throwing trash and waste into the river. Dirty water from drains also flows into it. The river water looks black and smells bad. They know this water is polluted. It is not safe for the fish, the plants or for people. Nusair and Samin feel sad and wonder, "Why do people make the river so dirty?"

As they walk, many cars and buses pass by. They see black smoke coming from the vehicles. This smoke pollutes the air. Breathing this polluted air can make people sick. The vehicles also honk their horns very loudly. It hurts their ears. Very often, they cover their ears with their hands. They feel uneasy for this sound pollution. They ask each other, "Why are the vehicles so loud?"

Nusair and Samin know that the world around us is very important. Clean air and water help us stay healthy. However, living a healthy life becomes impossible when people pollute the air, water, and make too much noise. They make a promise to each other. They will do their best to keep their environment clean and peaceful for everyone.

sections.instructionBn: Read the text again and answer the following questions in a sentence or sentences.

items.text: Where and how do Nusair and Samin go every morning?
items.answer: Every morning they go to Armanitola Government Primary School on foot (they walk) along the river Buriganga.

items.text: Why do Nusair and Samin feel sad?
items.answer: They feel sad because people throw trash and waste into the river and make the water polluted.

items.text: What can polluted air do to people?
items.answer: Breathing polluted air can make people sick.

items.text: How does sound pollution happen?
items.answer: Sound pollution happens when vehicles honk their horns very loudly.

items.text: What do Samin and Nusair promise to each other?
items.answer: They promise to do their best to keep their environment clean and peaceful for everyone.

items.text: Abdullah woke up **early** and prepared for Fajr prayer.

items.note: ‘adverb খুঁজে লেখ’ থেকে চিহ্নিত শব্দের পদ নির্ণয় করা হয়েছে

items.text: Write a paragraph about the importance of reading books.
items.answer: Marking points: a topic sentence; books give knowledge and joy; many kinds of books (story, science, religious, poetry); reading improves writing and speaking; reading regularly keeps body and mind healthy; good habit for free time; a library / book fair helps; a concluding sentence. About 8–10 simple, correct sentences.

items.text: Write a letter to your friend describing your hobby.
items.answer: Marking points (book’s letter format, Unit 10): address and date at the top right; salutation ‘Dear …,’; first paragraph — why you are writing; body — what the hobby is, when and how you do it, why you like it, what you have learnt; last paragraph — ask about the friend’s hobby / ask for a reply; closing (‘Your friend,’ / ‘Lots of love,’) and name.

authorNotes: Header check: the MP 2026 final file named "English_5.docx" prints "Class: Four" (the real Class 5 file prints "Class: Five" and has a different passage), so it IS the Class 4 annual paper and was used as the primary source. Its reading text is the Unit 15 ‘Environment Pollution’ text word for word, so it is a valid seen passage (Units 10–18). Reused from MP2026: the passage; its fill-in/true-false items turned into the 5 MCQs; its 5 short questions (2 marks → 1 mark); prepositions (Q8, verbatim); 6 verb-form items (Q11); 5 capitalization items (Q12); the paragraph (Q13) and the letter (Q14) — both are exactly topic (a) on the published lists; 10 of its 12 word meanings (Q4 — all 12 words are from Units 11–16; ‘Newspaper’ and ‘Welcome’ were dropped because the syllabus allows no ‘any ten’ choice). From other MP papers: sentence types (Final 2025 Q5 + HY 2026 Q5 — five types, two of each), articles with ‘x’ (Final 2025 Q3), 4 parts-of-speech items (Final 2025 Q4; its ‘on’, ‘and’, ‘Alas’ items were skipped because the row lists only noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun), 5 capitalization items (HY 2025 Q3). NEW: 8 question-making items from Unit 16 activity 4.2 / Unit 17, and 4 verb items for present perfect, present continuous and past continuous (Units 11, 15, 18). MP2026 sections with no Sylhet row (Bangla→English translation, sentence transformation) were not used except two interrogative items moved into the Yes/No row. Doubts for the owner: (1) Row 8 says ‘simple/indefinite, continuous and present perfect’; I read ‘continuous’ as present and past continuous (both are taught in Units 15 and 18) and kept MP’s simple past/future items as ‘simple/indefinite’. (2) Paragraph and letter are given as one fixed topic each (topic a), with no choice; if the school wants students to choose, add topic (b) and a choice note. (3) The passage sits only in section 1; section 2 refers back to it. (4) Duration not published; set to ৩ ঘণ্টা (MP printed 2 h 30 min).
